name: Li-ion Battery Current-Collector Foils: Aluminium & Copper Foil Localisation
scope: Battery-grade aluminium (cathode) and copper (anode) current-collector foil in India: demand, import dependence, policy (battery-component scheme, anti-dumping duty) and the listed companies building capacity.

summary.one_line: India imports an estimated 80-85% of its battery foil. Hindalco has commissioned capacity and SRF has just approved a plant, but demand depends on gigafactories that are mostly not built yet, and foil is a small revenue line for every listed producer.
key_points: IndexBox (May 2026) estimates imports cover 80-85% of India's battery-foil demand in 2026. China supplies 50-55% of import volume, Japan 20-25% and South Korea 10-15%. IndexBox projects 18-22% CAGR over 2026-2035, to 25,000-35,000 t and INR 2,500-4,000 cr by 2035 (S1).

Hindalco commissioned India's first battery-grade aluminium foil facility in Odisha on 27 Jan 2026. It sits inside a Rs 4,500 cr, 1.7 lakh tpa FRP complex and is designed to support up to 100 GWh of cell manufacturing (S3). The company's product page gives 25,000 t of annual capacity (S4).

On 21 Oct 2026 SRF's board approved a roughly Rs 600 cr battery-foil plant at SRF Altech's Jetapur (MP) site. It will be built in two phases of about Rs 300 cr each, with Phase I (12,000 MTPA) due by 30 Sep 2028 and Phase II by 30 Sep 2030 (S6). The plant targets lithium-ion and sodium-ion cells (S7).

Shyam Metalics said in 2023 that its 12-20 micron battery foil had been validated by third-party labs (S13). However, its 18,000 tpa Sambalpur foil plant, in commercial production since July 2026, is described as serving packaging, pharma and industrial uses (S14), and no battery-foil sales volumes have been disclosed (S15).

The roughly Rs 12,000-13,000 cr battery-materials scheme covers cathode, anode, separator, copper foil and electrolyte. Aluminium foil is not on the list (S9, S10). As of Sep-Oct 2026 the scheme was moving to the Expenditure Finance Committee and had not been notified (S9).

No listed Indian company produces copper battery foil yet. Hindalco holds a Nippon Denkai technology licence for electrodeposited copper foil (S11), and ICICI Direct says it is building a battery copper-foil plant (S10). No capacity has been confirmed in the company documents reviewed for this report.

Anti-dumping duty on aluminium foil of 80 microns and below from China, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand has been extended to 15 Dec 2026 while DGTR completes a sunset review. Hindalco and SRF Altech are among the applicants (S16).

Demand is lagging. Of 50 GWh under ACC-PLI, 40 GWh has been awarded but only 1 GWh had been commissioned as of Mar 2026 (S18). IndexBox's 2030 demand estimate of 12,000-16,000 t (S1) is below Hindalco's capacity alone (S4).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Hindalco is first mover: its plant is commissioned and fed directly from its own FRP complex (S3). It has supplied battery foil since 2018 and says it serves customers in Europe, the USA, Asia and India (S4).

SRF is building on an existing aluminium-foil platform at Jetapur, approved in 2022 at 21,000 MTPA for Rs 425 cr (S8). Its foil plant is also protected by anti-dumping duty, which SRF Altech petitioned to continue (S16).
If the battery-materials scheme is notified with copper foil in scope, Hindalco is the only listed name with a disclosed copper-foil technology licence (S10, S11).
Sodium-ion chemistry uses aluminium foil on both electrodes, needing an estimated 700-1,000 t per GWh against 350-500 t for lithium-ion (S17). SRF has explicitly targeted sodium-ion (S7).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Announced aluminium-foil capacity runs ahead of near-term domestic demand. Hindalco's 25,000 t (S4) plus SRF's 12,000 t Phase I (S6) compares with IndexBox's 12,000-16,000 t for 2030 (S1). Hindalco's own forecast of 40,000 t by 2030 is higher (S5).
The anti-dumping duty lapses on 15 Dec 2026 unless the sunset review recommends continuation (S16). China supplies 50-55% of India's battery-foil imports (S1).
Foil is immaterial to group revenue. IndexBox's entire 2035 India battery-foil market of INR 2,500-4,000 cr (S1) is about 3-5% of Hindalco's Q1 FY27 quarterly revenue of Rs 84,825 cr (S22).
Gigafactory delays: only 1 GWh of the 40 GWh awarded under ACC-PLI had been commissioned by Mar 2026 (S18). Qualification takes a minimum of a few months per sample across several stages (S2).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: DGTR final findings in the aluminium-foil sunset review, and any customs notification before 15 Dec 2026 (S16).
EFC and Cabinet approval and notification of the battery-materials scheme, especially whether aluminium foil is added (S9).
Hindalco Q2 FY27 commentary on Aditya battery-foil utilisation and named cell-maker qualifications (S22, S4).
Whether Shyam Metalics discloses any battery-foil volumes or customers from its Sambalpur foil plant (S14, S15).

sections.title: What battery foil is and why India imports it

blocks.text: In a lithium-ion cell, aluminium foil is the cathode current collector and copper foil is the anode current collector (S2, S9). IndexBox gives typical aluminium battery foil as 12-15 µm thick, with thinning targets of 12-15 µm for aluminium and 6 µm and below for copper. Standard electrodeposited copper is 8-10 µm, and ultra-thin 6 µm copper carries a ±1 µm tolerance (S1). Swarajya puts electrodeposited copper foil at 4.5-8 µm (S9). Chinese industry sources say power-battery aluminium foil is mostly 20, 15, 13 or 12 µm, and moving toward 10 µm and below (S17). Hindalco has developed four battery-grade alloys, including AA1100 and AA1060 (S4).

Qualification is set by the customer. Hindalco says each sample needs a minimum of a few months of testing across several stages (S2). IndexBox notes that buyers expect certificates covering tensile strength, elongation, surface roughness and thickness uniformity (S1). It also says existing small-scale domestic foil generally fails the thickness-tolerance, roughness and ductility specifications that battery electrodes require (S1).

blocks.text: The ~4-5% bill-of-materials figure comes from Hindalco, a producer (S2). A Chinese trade source puts aluminium foil alone at 1.5-2.0% of Li-ion cost (S17). Neither source explains its basis, so both are shown and treated as indicative only.

IndexBox (report updated 1 May 2026) estimates that imports meet 80-85% of India's battery-foil demand in 2026, with China at 50-55% of import volume, Japan at 20-25% and South Korea at 10-15% (S1). Its own text is inconsistent on domestic supply, putting it at both under 20% and under 10% of demand (S1). IndexBox forecasts 12,000-16,000 t by 2030 and 25,000-35,000 t (INR 2,500-4,000 cr) by 2035, with a bull case above 40,000 t and a bear case of 15,000-18,000 t (S1). Hindalco's own forecast is higher, at 40,000 t of battery-grade aluminium-foil demand by 2030 (S5).

Downstream demand depends on cell plants. Under ACC-PLI (outlay INR 18,100 cr), 40 GWh of the 50 GWh target had been awarded by Mar 2026: Ola Electric 20 GWh, Reliance New Energy 15 GWh and Rajesh Exports 5 GWh. Only 1 GWh, Ola's, had been commissioned (S18). India imported USD 4.93 bn of lithium-ion batteries in 2025-26, of which 93.79% came from China (S9).

subsections.title: Battery-materials incentive scheme and trade protection

items: Size: about Rs 12,000 cr according to The Economic Times as cited by Outlook Business in Jun 2026, which described it as in the final stages of approval (S10). Swarajya, in Sep 2026 (updated Oct 2026), puts it at about Rs 12,000-13,000 cr (S9).
Scope: cathode, anode, separator, copper foil and electrolyte (S9, S10). Neither source lists aluminium foil. In May 2025 Hindalco said no PLI covered its aluminium-foil project (S2).

Status: Swarajya reports the scheme is with the Ministry of Heavy Industries, is moving to the finance ministry's Expenditure Finance Committee, and has not been notified (S9). Swarajya also estimates that announced cathode and anode plants alone need Rs 30,000-35,000 cr of capex, about three times the scheme's envelope (S9).

Anti-dumping: duty on aluminium foil of 80 microns and below from China, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, originally under Notification 51/2021-Customs (ADD), was extended to 15 Dec 2026. DGTR started the sunset review on 29 Sep 2025 and held an oral hearing on 28 Apr; Hindalco and SRF Altech are among the applicants (S16).

blocks.text: Aluminium-foil producers (Hindalco, SRF, Shyam Metalics) are not named beneficiaries of the battery-materials scheme in the sources reviewed. Their main policy lever is the anti-dumping duty, which expires on 15 Dec 2026 (S9, S16).

subsections.title: Hindalco: commissioned, but small relative to the group

blocks.text: Hindalco says the battery-grade aluminium foil facility commissioned on 27 Jan 2026 is India's first of its kind. It draws input directly from the 1.7 lakh tpa FRP complex (Rs 4,500 cr combined) and is designed to support up to 100 GWh of cells (S3). The company's product page cites a USD 100 mn cathode-foil facility with 25,000 t of annual capacity, a 2,400 t customer-qualification line near Nagpur, and an upgraded Mouda foil mill with a battery slitter and test labs (S4). Hindalco has not named any qualified cell makers. It says it has supplied customers across Europe, the USA, Asia and India (S4), and its 2023 release said Mouda was qualifying with cell makers in India, Europe and the US (S5). The Q1 FY27 update lists the Aditya battery-foil plant among commissioned projects but gives no volumes (S22).

Materiality is low. Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue was Rs 84,825 cr, and downstream aluminium revenue was Rs 4,889 cr (S22). IndexBox's entire 2035 Indian battery-foil market of INR 2,500-4,000 cr (S1) is equal to about 3-5% of one quarter of Hindalco's revenue (our arithmetic).

On copper foil, Nippon Denkai signed a Technology License and Support Agreement with Hindalco for electrodeposited Li-ion copper foil in India, with an initial payment and royalties tied to Hindalco's sales (S11). Birla's Rs 45,000 cr commitment (Mar 2025) was reported to include India's first EV copper-foil plant (S12). ICICI Direct says Hindalco is setting up a battery copper-foil plant (S10), and Swarajya reports an 11,500 t plant at Waghodia, Gujarat (S9). In May 2025 Hindalco described copper foil as early-stage (S2), and none of the Hindalco pages reviewed give a copper-foil capacity.

SRF's 21 Oct 2026 approval is a project under its wholly owned subsidiary SRF Altech at the existing Jetapur, MP site, funded through debt and internal accruals. The filing frames it as adding future-ready, value-added products for energy storage and EVs (S6). It extends the 21,000 MTPA aluminium-foil plant at Jaitapur, Indore, approved in Jan 2022 for Rs 425 cr (S8). In Q2 FY27, SRF's Performance Films & Foil segment revenue rose 51% to Rs 2,122 cr, against consolidated revenue of Rs 4,904 cr (S7). At SMM's Dec 2025 China price of about USD 4,599/t for 12 µm battery foil (S24), 12,000 t would be worth roughly USD 55 mn a year at full utilisation (our arithmetic, illustrative).

Shyam Metalics announced battery-grade foil in Sep 2023, with 12-20 µm product validated by third-party labs and overall foil capacity of 20,000 t/yr. It gave no battery-specific capacity (S13). Its 18,000 tpa Sambalpur foil plant (6-40 µm) began commercial production on 16 Jul 2026 and is described as serving packaging, pharma and industrial uses (S14). A Jun 2026 investor update says the aluminium division is expanding with battery-foil capability, that foil utilisation is 90% and that exports exceed 60% of output, but it gives no battery volumes (S15).

No disclosed source confirms that Shyam Metalics sells battery-grade foil commercially or in what volume. It is placed in the commissioned bucket because its foil capacity is operating and it claims battery-grade capability (S13, S14, S15).

subsections.title: Has the market priced it in?

blocks.title: Share-price returns to 23 Oct 2026
blocks.source: Source: ICICIdirect quote pages (S19, S20, S21)

blocks.text: Share-price moves do not track the foil theme. Hindalco is down 16.35% over six months (S19) and SRF is down 24.94% over one year (S20). Shyam Metalics is up 39.23% over six months (S21) and hit an all-time high above Rs 30,000 cr market cap when the foil plant was commissioned (S14). Coverage is thin. ICICI Direct named Hindalco as a potential beneficiary in a battery-component note (S10), and DSIJ ran a 2023 piece on Shyam's battery foil (S23). Our searches found no dedicated broker thematic on 'battery foil stocks'.

blocks.text: IndexBox's 'top participants' list names companies such as Exide, Tata AutoComp and Mahindra as foil players. This conflicts with its own text, which says no large-scale domestic foil plant operates, so those names are not used here (S1).

items: Trade: the Al-foil anti-dumping duty expires on 15 Dec 2026 pending the DGTR sunset review (S16). Chinese copper-foil overcapacity, about 2.1 mn t against about 1 mn t of demand, can depress prices (S9).
Demand timing: 1 GWh of 40 GWh awarded under ACC-PLI had been commissioned by Mar 2026 (S18). IndexBox does not expect domestic commercial output in several states before 2028-29 (S1).
Overcapacity: Hindalco's 25,000 t (S4) plus SRF's 12,000 t (S6) exceeds IndexBox's 2030 demand of 12,000-16,000 t (S1), which would make exports necessary.
Qualification: testing takes a minimum of a few months per sample over several stages (S2), and no named cell-maker approvals have been disclosed (S4).
Policy: the battery-materials scheme has not been notified and excludes aluminium foil in reported drafts (S9, S10).
Materiality: foil is a small part of revenue for all three producers (S1, S7, S22).

companies.name: Hindalco Industries
companies.role: Commissioned India's first battery-grade aluminium foil facility (Aditya, Odisha, Jan 2026), with 25,000 tpa capacity supporting ~100 GWh and a 2,400 t qualification line near Nagpur (S3, S4). Holds a Nippon Denkai licence for electrodeposited copper foil (S11).
companies.impact: First mover protected by anti-dumping duty (S16) and the only listed name with a copper-foil route into the pending scheme (S10). Foil is immaterial against quarterly revenue of Rs 84,825 cr (S22), and the stock is down 16.35% over six months (S19).

companies.name: Shyam Metalics and Energy
companies.role: Aluminium foil producer. Announced third-party-validated 12-20 µm battery foil in 2023 (S13). Started a 18,000 tpa, 6-40 µm foil plant at Sambalpur in Jul 2026 aimed at packaging, pharma and industrial uses (S14).
companies.impact: Says it has battery-foil capability, but has disclosed no battery volumes or customers. Foil runs at 90% utilisation with more than 60% exported (S15). The stock is up 39.23% over six months (S21), driven more by group expansion than battery foil.

companies.name: SRF
companies.role: Board approved a ~Rs 600 cr battery aluminium-foil plant via SRF Altech at Jetapur, MP: 12,000 MTPA Phase I by Sep 2028 and Phase II by Sep 2030 (S6), for Li-ion and sodium-ion cells (S7). It builds on a 21,000 MTPA foil plant approved in 2022 (S8).
companies.impact: Adjacent to its Performance Films & Foil segment (Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 2,122 cr) (S7). Depends on anti-dumping duty continuation (S16) and gigafactory demand from 2028. The stock is down 24.94% over one year (S20).

companies.name: Ola Electric Mobility
companies.role: ACC-PLI beneficiary with 20 GWh awarded and the only commissioned capacity (1 GWh) as of Mar 2026 (S18). IndexBox says Ola Cell Technologies is exploring backward integration into foil (S1).
companies.impact: Its cell ramp-up is the largest single driver of domestic foil demand. Any in-house foil plan would compete with merchant suppliers (S1, S18).

companies.name: Reliance Industries
companies.role: Reliance New Energy holds 15 GWh under ACC-PLI (S18). IndexBox names it as exploring backward integration into foil production (S1).
companies.impact: A potential large foil buyer, or a captive producer if it integrates. No company-confirmed foil plan was found (S1, S18).

companies.name: Rajesh Exports
companies.impact: Foil demand from it depends on its gigafactory being commissioned, which had not happened as of Mar 2026 (S18).

companies.name: HEG
companies.role: Setting up a graphite anode facility. ICICI Direct sees it as a potential beneficiary of the same battery-materials scheme that covers copper foil (S10).
companies.impact: Adjacent, not a foil maker: notification of the scheme would move anode and copper-foil names together (S10).

companies.name: Graphite India
companies.role: Signed an MoU with Maharashtra for a synthetic-graphite anode project. ICICI Direct names it a potential scheme beneficiary (S10).
companies.impact: Adjacent, not a foil maker: exposed to the same scheme approval timing (S9, S10).

method: First edition, researched on 25-26 Oct 2026 with web search and direct page fetches. Primary and company sources used: Hindalco press releases and product page, SRF's NSE filing (seen in search results; fetch timed out) and results coverage, and Shyam Metalics announcements. IndexBox is used for market sizing, and Outlook Business / Swarajya for scheme status and the ICICI Direct view. Share-price returns come from ICICIdirect quote pages timestamped 23 Oct 2026. numbers.json was not present in the folder. Claims that could not be confirmed were dropped or flagged, including Hindalco's copper-foil capacity, Shyam's battery-foil volumes, named cell-maker qualifications, and the DGTR final finding. Companies were searched across small, mid and large caps. No small-cap listed battery-foil producer was found, so the extra names are cell makers (foil demand) and battery-materials scheme peers (adjacent), each labelled as 'other'. 'Our arithmetic' marks simple derived figures. No ratings or price targets.
